subject: Connector compatibility & SKU mapping for multi-cloud marketplace listing
messages:
From: Devon Park <devon@cogworks.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cogworks.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace connector compatibility + SKU mapping questions

Hi Monica —

Thanks again for taking a look. We are preparing our multi-cloud connector bundle for AWS Marketplace, GCP Marketplace, and Azure Marketplace listings. A few quick items we want to confirm before the certification run next week: 

1) Compatibility matrix: our connector package includes a native AWS Lambda-based adapter, a GCP Cloud Run container, and an Azure Function shim. Are there Redwood-specific expectations for runtime hooks or telemetry endpoints we must expose for the co-sell telemetry integration?

2) SKU mapping: we attached a draft SKU spreadsheet (sku-mapping-draft.xlsx). Redwood has different catalog SKUs for hosted vs dedicated vs private. What naming format will reduce approval friction and avoid manual remapping on your side?

3) Metering & agent placement: for metered billing on AWS we expect to deploy a lightweight agent in the VPC; does Redwood require any special configuration for prefix-caching or request routing that would affect the agent's placement?

4) Evidence + packaging: we attached the connector binaries (cogworks_connectors_v1.2.zip). Will you need FedRAMP / SOC evidence up front for the listing, or can that be included during listing review?

Would you be able to loop in the right Redwood folks on co-sell readiness and the SKU template? We want to avoid rework during your marketplace intake.

Thanks —
Devon
Devon Park
Head of Partnerships, CogWorks
devon@cogworks.io
https://cogworks.io

Attachment: cogworks_connectors_v1.2.zip (archive, 18 MB)
Attachment: sku-mapping-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@cogworks.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace connector compatibility + SKU mapping questions

Thanks Devon — this is helpful and timely. Looping in Vivek and Olga from our alliances/ops teams so they can triage technical dependencies and the SKU naming.

Quick answers to unblock you: 
- We don't need runtime telemetry endpoints beyond standard request logs; however, co-sell telemetry requires a small tagging header (X-Redwood-Partner) on calls that hit hosted instances so we can aggregate attribution.
- For SKU names, a single canonical SKU per product variant (hosted / dedicated / private) is preferred; Vivek will share a naming template.
- Metering agent placement: we generally accept an agent inside the VPC but need the agent to emit a heartbeat and be reachable for lightweight callbacks during billing reconciliation.
- SOC 2 evidence can be attached in the listing review step; FedRAMP is separate and only required for specific public-sector listings.

Propose a 30-minute triage tomorrow at 10am PT to go over the sheet and the connector zip. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Park <devon@cogworks.io>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace connector compatibility + SKU mapping questions

Hi Devon / Monica —

I did a quick pass on the attachments and sketched specific asks so our certification and co-sell teams can move fast. Below are action items and a lightweight checklist we need before the intake: 

Technical checklist (pre-cert)
- Container images must accept REDWOOD_PARTNER_TAG header and expose /healthz and /metrics endpoints.
- GCP: service account must include roles/cloudfunctions.invoker or Cloud Run invoker role depending on deployment. If using Cloud Run, please provide the container digest (sha256) for immutable reference.
- Azure: include App Registration ID and indicate if you need Managed Identity access to resources in customer subscriptions.
- Agent: heartbeat interval >= 60s and callback endpoint must support TLS 1.2+.

SKU naming guidance (attached template):
- Format: partnerCode.productName.variant.region (e.g., CW.Cortex.hosted.us)
- Avoid special characters; use lower-case and '.' separators.
- One canonical SKU per supported deployment mode; we will create aliases for marketplace-specific SKUs during ingestion.

Metering notes:
- For AWS metering, use server-side tracking with the agent emitting usage batches; avoid relying solely on prefix-caching for billing events. This reduces reconciliation differences.

Evidence & timeline:
- SOC 2 Type II report will suffice for standard enterprise listings; FedRAMP conversation can be parallel but is not a blocker for most cloud marketplace entries.

I've attached the SKU naming template and a short intake checklist we use for partner submissions. Let's take the triage meeting today at 10am PT as Monica suggested. If you can share the Cloud Run digest and the Azure App Registration ID beforehand that will save 10–15 minutes.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_sku_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: partner_intake_checklist.pdf (pdf)

All — thanks for the checklist and the template, that cleared a lot up. Quick updates before the 10am PT call: 

- Cloud Run: digest is sha256:4b2f7a... (we'll paste full digest into the Drive folder).
- Azure: App Registration ID is 9b7f-11a3; we do require a Managed Identity option for enterprise installs.
- Agent: will be updated to emit heartbeat every 90s and support TLS 1.2+.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II in progress; estimated delivery Oct 12. Not a blocker for our initial listing.

We'll join the 10am PT triage with our engineer (Alyssa) and will upload the full connector digest and a trimmed-down architecture diagram to the Drive link you provided.

See you shortly —
Devon
